pages.name: cm² to mm²
pages.task: A rating plate is 5 cm by 4 cm, so it covers 20 cm². How many mm² is that?
pages.why: Each cm² holds 10 × 10 = 100 mm², so 20 cm² is 20 × 100 = 2,000 mm². In mm the plate is 50 mm by 40 mm, and 50 × 40 = 2,000 mm² too.

pages.name: Square metres
pages.text: A 1 m square is 100 cm each way. One row of 1 cm squares along the bottom is only 100 cm². With 100 rows, 1 m² is 10,000 cm².
pages.alt: A 1 metre square, 100 centimetres each way, with a ruler of centimetres along the bottom and up the side. One row of 1 centimetre squares along the bottom is 100 square centimetres. 100 rows of 100 are filled. Each 10 centimetre square of the grid is 10 times 10, 100 square centimetres. 100 times 100 equals 10,000 square centimetres.

pages.name: m² to cm²
pages.task: A switch room floor is 3 m by 2 m, so it covers 6 m². How many cm² is that?
pages.why: Each m² is 100 × 100 = 10,000 cm², so 6 m² is 6 × 10,000 = 60,000 cm². In cm the floor is 300 cm by 200 cm, and 300 × 200 = 60,000 cm² too.

pages.name: Four times the area
pages.task: Drag the corner to draw a square with 4 times the area of the shaded 10 cm square.
pages.why: Twice the side fits 2 × 2 = 4 copies, so the square is 20 cm by 20 cm, 400 cm². Four times the side would fit 4 × 4 = 16 copies.

pages.name: Any shape
pages.text: Any shape made twice as long every way covers 4 times the area. A triangle holds 4 copies, one turned round. A round wire twice as wide has 4 times the [[cross-section]].

pages.name: Three times the sides
pages.task: A triangular plate covers 600 cm². What does a plate the same shape cover with every side 3 times as long?
pages.why: Every side is 3 times as long, so 3 × 3 = 9 copies of the small plate fit inside. 9 × 600 = 5,400 cm².

pages.text: Cable sizes are areas. Nexans lists 1.5 mm² to 35 mm², sizes set by IEC 60228. A 35 mm² size means an area of 35 of these 1 mm squares.

pages.name: mm² to cm²
pages.task: A conductor's cross-section is 25 mm². How many cm² is that?
pages.why: 1 cm² is 100 mm², so 25 mm² is 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 cm², a quarter of the 1 cm square.

pages.name: m² to mm²
pages.task: 1 m is 1,000 mm. How many mm² make 1 m²?
pages.why: A 1 m square is 1,000 mm each way, so it holds 1,000 rows of 1,000 square millimetres. That is 1,000 × 1,000 = 1,000,000 mm².
pages.alt: A 1 metre square, 1,000 millimetres each way, ruled in 100 millimetre squares, with a ruler along the bottom and up the side. One 100 millimetre square holds 10,000 square millimetres, and the whole square fills: 1,000 times 1,000 equals 1,000,000 square millimetres.

pages.name: A copper bar
pages.task: A flat copper bar is 30 mm wide and 5 mm thick. What is its cross-section in cm²?
pages.why: 30 × 5 = 150 mm², and 150 ÷ 100 = 1.5 cm². In cm the bar is 3 cm by 0.5 cm, and 3 × 0.5 = 1.5 cm² too.
